operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are backtick-quoted in DDL; generated SQL must double-quote them; table names are mixed-case (Problem_Log, Problem_Category_Codes) and must be preserved verbatim.
Tiny DB: every table has 2-15 rows; original_values lists are complete, so no rowid sampling needed but read_schema must still handle max_rows_per_table.
DATETIME columns store TEXT like '2011-03-13 13:11:57' (space separator, no T, no fractional seconds); storage class text contradicts declared DATETIME.
DATETIME columns dispatch to 'Date|Number(int elements)' — first element '2011-03-13 13:11:57' does NOT parse as int, so Date fuzzer with template %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.
All VARCHAR columns store short text; several hold single letters ('t','a','b') and one holds a typo 'Datatabase' — literal pool will be tiny and noisy.

Problem_Log has 4 FKs to 4 different parents (Problem_Category_Codes, Problem_Status_Codes, Staff, Problems); Problems has 2 FKs to Staff (closure_authorised_by_staff_id, reported_by_staff_id) — same parent, two child columns.
FK graph: Staff, Product, Problem_Category_Codes, Problem_Status_Codes are level-0; Problems depends on Staff+Product; Problem_Log depends on all four — no cycles, no self-FKs.
All FKs point to existing parents with single-column INTEGER/VARCHAR PKs; no dangling FKs, no composite keys, no non-unique parents.

NOT NULL on FK columns (assigned_to_staff_id, problem_id, problem_category_code, problem_status_code, product_id, closure_authorised_by_staff_id, reported_by_staff_id, date_problem_reported) — TS does not enforce NOT NULL in Python, so NULL FK draws will fail at insert and be skipped.
PKs are single-column INTEGER (autoincrement-like) or VARCHAR(20); no composite PKs, no UNIQUE constraints beyond PK.
No CHECK constraints, no views, no triggers, no indexes beyond PK in DDL.
date_problem_closed is nullable but null_rate 0.0 in original — TS may still emit NULLs there (Date fuzzer with p>0 returns elements, not NULLs, so likely fine).
operator_ts_expectations: String fuzzer on VARCHAR(20/80/255) columns: fresh random strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() of length 0-20 (or 0-255 for VARCHAR(255) via args[0]) plus 5 sampled originals + literal-pool values; contaminate 50% of the time — produces implausible names like 'xq3()' for staff_first_name.

Date fuzzer on DATETIME columns: template %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S, range from min/max of parsed originals (1973-2013), p=0.2 means 20% element reuse, 80% fresh uniform dates — plausible format but random years.

Number fuzzer on INTEGER PKs: range [-10^0, 10^0] = [-1,1] for scale 0 (INTEGER has no args → scale 0), so PKs are tiny ints perturbed by ±1/±2 — collides heavily, sample_fresh_primary_keys drops duplicates, shrinking tables.

Number fuzzer on INTEGER FK columns: same tiny range, but FK fill draws from parent's already-generated values with replacement — so FK values are valid but heavily duplicated (distinct 9-11 in original, TS will produce fewer).
FK fill: Problem_Log.problem_id draws from Problems.problem_id AFTER Problems PK dedup — if Problems shrinks to 1-2 rows, Problem_Log FK has almost no variety.
String fuzzer on VARCHAR PKs (problem_category_code, problem_status_code): fresh random strings + 5 originals + pool; PK dedup drops most, leaving ~3-5 rows — matches original cardinality by luck.
Literal pool from train SQL: tiny DB, few queries, pool will be sparse; most columns fall back to 5 originals + fresh draws.

Likely FN driver: String fuzzer produces implausible values (random chars) for name/description columns, so queries filtering on real names ('Lacey') return empty in TS instances → gold non-empty, TS empty → FN.
Likely FP driver: Number fuzzer's tiny range [-1,1] on INTEGER columns makes many rows share values, so COUNT/aggregate queries may coincidentally match gold on degenerate instances → FP.
Date fuzzer's 80% fresh uniform dates over 1973-2013 range means date-range predicates (BETWEEN) will often match by chance → possible FP on date filters.
No CHECK/NOT NULL enforcement in Python: NULL FK draws (when parent empty) fail insert and are skipped, silently shrinking Problem_Log/Problems — TS may produce empty child tables.
